verdicts.claim: SQLite automatically triggers a checkpoint when the WAL file reaches a threshold of 1000 pages by default.
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.1: 'By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.' (litestream page does not state it; its 1000 is Litestream's own min-checkpoint-page-count)

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE checkpointing is a non-blocking, best-effort operation that copies as many frames as possible without waiting for rea
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish'

verdicts.claim: FULL checkpointing blocks (invokes the busy-handler) until all readers are reading from the most recent snapshot and no wr
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames'

verdicts.claim: RESTART checkpointing behaves like FULL but additionally blocks until all readers are reading from the main database file
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL ... blocks ... until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.'

verdicts.claim: TRUNCATE checkpointing behaves like RESTART but also truncates the WAL file to zero bytes upon successful completion.
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.'

verdicts.claim: Read performance degrades as the WAL file size increases because readers must check the WAL for the most recent versions
verdicts.evidence: wal.html §2.3: 'read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows in size since each reader must check the WAL file for the content' (sqlite.work does not address it)

verdicts.claim: All checkpoint modes obtain an exclusive 'checkpoint' lock; FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE additionally obtain an exclusive '
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: 'All calls obtain an exclusive "checkpoint" lock ... The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive "writer" lock'

verdicts.claim: The TRUNCATE mode performs an ftruncate to zero bytes rather than unlinking the WAL file from the filesystem.
verdicts.evidence: vellum PR #34986: TRUNCATE 'only truncates the WAL to zero bytes (ftruncate, not unlink)'; c3ref says 'truncates the log file to zero bytes' but does not name ftruncate/unlink

verdicts.claim: Long-lived read transactions maintain historical snapshots of the database, preventing checkpoints from progressing beyon
verdicts.evidence: sqlite.work: 'Checkpointing cannot proceed beyond the earliest active snapshot'; wal.html: 'a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress'
